key_insight: UA-ChatDev improves multi-agent software development by estimating uncertainty in agent outputs and only adding verification when confidence is low, reducing error propagation across development stages.
engineering_relevance: This is relevant for building more reliable LLM-based coding pipelines, especially where early-stage mistakes can cascade into broken requirements, code, or tests.
method: Uses token-level log probabilities to estimate response uncertainty for each agent.
Applies phase-aware threshold calibration to decide when retrieval-based verification should be triggered.
Coordinates multi-agent collaboration for requirements analysis, coding, testing, and refinement with uncertainty-aware communication.
evidence_signal: Experiments on the SRDD benchmark show improvements over existing single-agent and multi-agent frameworks on completeness, executability, consistency, and overall quality, with ablations supporting the benefit of uncertainty-aware interactions.
watch_item: The approach depends on well-calibrated uncertainty estimates and retrieval quality, so threshold tuning and added verification overhead may affect robustness and latency.
paper_title: UA-ChatDev: Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Agent Collaboration for Reliable Software Development
